display.title: Where Has My Story Gone? Part 2
display.summary_short: Reb Yaakov finally remembers one story: the day the Baal Shem Tov summoned a bishop from his platform. His host's reaction reveals why every other story was forgotten.
display.summary_long: After the song "I believe in Hashem" and a recap, Reb Yaakov tells his host in Rome the only story he can remember. Ten years earlier, before Pesach, the Baal Shem Tov left right after Havdalah and let the horses lead them to an unfamiliar city on a day of a non-Jewish festival, when Jews feared to go outside. From a Jewish home he watched the marketplace, where a bishop was to give a fiery speech against the Jews. He sent Reb Yaakov through the crowd to tell the bishop, in Yiddish, that the Baal Shem Tov wanted him. The bishop calmly promised to come after his speech, but when Reb Yaakov returned a second time, the bishop went pale, stopped his speech, and met the Baal Shem Tov privately. Hearing this, Reb Moshe dances for joy: he was that bishop. A gifted yeshiva student, he had left home for university, dropped his mitzvos one by one, and risen in the church, but felt empty. The Baal Shem Tov came to him in dreams, guided his teshuvah, and told him the sign of complete forgiveness would be someone telling him this very story. Reb Yaakov's forgetting had pushed him to strengthen his teshuvah, and in gratitude he gives Reb Yaakov half his wealth.
display.lesson: A Jew can always return to Hashem, and teshuvah is accepted in an instant; a tzaddik cares for every Jew and guides even those who have strayed far.

advisories.note: Jews fear violence on a non-Jewish festival when a bishop preaches against them.
Reb Yaakov is warned he may be attacked in the crowd; nothing happens.
